stem:
Inder wants a fair comparison of two household liquids using one prepared red-rose extract as the indicator. He also has turmeric paper from another lesson. He will use a dropper and may later label samples acid or base.

Which plan makes that comparison fair?

options.text: Use the same rose extract for both, add comparable amounts of each liquid with a dropper, and record the final colour for each sample.
Use one drop of sample A and ten drops of sample B; the test is still fair if the indicator is the same.
If both samples can later be labelled acid or base, the comparison must have been fair no matter how it was done.
Keeping turmeric paper for a different lesson makes today's rose-extract comparison unfair.

teacher.key_rationale: A fair test uses the same indicator, comparable amounts, and recorded final colours.
